title: GitHub Trending Weekly #12: AlohaMini, ZAPI, cgpu, Z-Image, F1 Race Replay, s&box, corner-shape

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Today, we're diving into GitHub Trending Weekly number 12, where we're exploring 24 of the hottest open-source projects that are taking the GitHub community by storm this week. Let's get started.

sections.title: AlohaMini
paragraphs: Aloha Mini, the DIY robot that looks like it escaped from a Google Deep Mind lab, but you can actually build it at home in about an hour. This thing is a dual arm mobile robot with a full motorized vertical lift. So, it can literally go from the floor to the table and manipulate objects across different heights like a tiny warehouse worker. It's loaded with five cameras, top view, front, back, and one on each arm.

sections.title: ZAPI
paragraphs: Zapi, the open- source tool that basically rips the API secrets out of any web app automatically. Zappy spins up Playright powered browser sessions, injects your O tokens, watches every network call, and captures the entire workflow, logs, traffic, all without you lifting a finger. Then it filters out the junk. No images, no CSS, just pure APIs, cleanly extracted with cost and time estimates before you process anything.

sections.title: cgpu
paragraphs: Stop wishing you had a GPU? CGPU gives you one right in your terminal for free. This CLI lets you spin up free cloud GPUs instantly, so you can actually learn CUDA C++ without buying a $1,500 graphics card or waiting in a queue for half an hour. Just run the command, get a GPU, and start compiling. No infrastructure, no credit card, no nonsense.

sections.title: Z-Image
paragraphs: Zimage 6 billion parameter foundation model proving you don't need a monster GPU to get worldclass image generation. Through smart systematic optimization, Zimage delivers photorealistic quality and bilingual text rendering that rivals models 10 times its size. And it runs smoothly on consumer GPUs under 16 GB. That means high-end generation is now accessible to everyone.

sections.title: F1 Race Replay
paragraphs: Love F1, but wish you could relive races like a director? Meet F1 Race Replay, a Python app that turns raw telemetry into a cinematic interactive replay. Watch drivers slice around a rendered track in real time. Follow the live leaderboard with tire compounds and see retirements flagged as out the moment they happen. Want details? Click a driver to pull up telemetry. Speed, current lap, all at your fingertips.

sections.title: UptimeKit
paragraphs: Uptime kit, a sleek uptime monitor that lives in your terminal but behaves like a full monitoring stack. Spin it up and it runs as a background demon so your checks keep running even when your terminal is closed. Need a quick status peak? Open the live TUI dashboard for real-time health, latency, uptime percentages, and handy P95 stats, complete with latency spark lines and a status history timeline.

sections.title: corner-shape
paragraphs: Corner shape, a Tailwind plugin that brings first class utilities for the brand new CSS corner shape property. Yes, per corner shapes like corner top left shape right in your utility kit. Want a scoop, a notch, a squirle, or a precise super ellipse corner? This plugin generates utilities for the static keywords round, scoop, bevel, notch, square, squirle, and the functional value super ellipse.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: This is for everyone who doomscrolls at 2 a.m. clicking on random islands asking, "What even is this place?" Because someone finally built the tool we all needed. It's called history, and it lets you click anywhere on a 3D globe. any island, mountain, tiny Arctic village with like nine people and it will actually research the entire history of that location for you. Actual research across historical archives, academic papers, and the modern web for up to 10 minutes.

sections.title: FLUX.2
paragraphs: Flux2, a massive 32 billion parameter rectified flow transformer. This model doesn't just create images from text. It can edit them, combine them, and follow complex instructions with state-of-the-art accuracy. What makes it wild is the no finetuning magic. You can give it a single character reference, an object, even a specific art style, and it nails it. No extra training, no Lauras, nothing. It's all built into one unified model. Essenbox is now an open- source game engine, and it's built on Valve's Source 2 and Modern.NET.

sections.title: s&box
paragraphs: You can create your own games in modern C with a super clean editor, instant play testing, and blazing fast hotloading. No compiling, no restarts. It even has visual scripting with action graph, shader graph, and a massive cloud asset library you can drag straight into your scene.

sections.title: smartcommit
paragraphs: Stop writing boring, loweffort commit messages. Let me show you smart commit, your AI powered commit message assistant. You stage your changes and smart commit instantly scans your git diff. But it doesn't stop at what changed. It actually asks you why you made the change. So instead of vague messages like update stuff, you get clean, perfect, conventional commits every time.

sections.title: Infidex
paragraphs: Infidex, it's a high performance.net search engine built on pattern recognition and it basically learns how to search from your own data. Infidex automatically analyzes your data set, extracts patterns like frequency and rarity, and maps everything into a multi-dimensional hypersphere. That means you get fuzzy querying with extreme typo tolerance without touching a single config file.

sections.title: EGGROLL in C
paragraphs: Someone just trained a language model in pure C with no floats, no GPUs, and no PyTorch. This project is a fully dependency-free implementation of the egg roll optimization algorithm and it trains a tiny LLM using integer only math. We're talking innate weights in 32 accumulation and zero back prop. Instead, it uses an evolutionary strategy. Low rank perturbations score the results evolve again.

sections.title: Agent SOP
paragraphs: Agent SOP, the secret sauce that makes AI agents actually reliable. Think of them as standard operating procedures, but written in natural language and built for AI. They're markdown based workflows that tell agents exactly what to do, how to do it, and what constraints they must follow, literally using RFC 2119 language like must, should, and may.

sections.title: Person Tracker Card
paragraphs: Want to know exactly where everyone in your household is without opening 10 apps? Meet person tracker card for home assistant. It's an advanced dashboard card with two layout modes. Classic for full customization or compact for a space-saving grid. Keep tabs on phone and smartwatch batteries. See real-time activity, walking, running, driving, cycling, and track distance from home with ways integration.

sections.title: Tabular Review for Lawyers
paragraphs: Tabular review, an AI powered document workspace that transforms messy legal documents into structured queryable data sets. Automatically extract key clauses, dates, amounts, and entities using Gemini while preserving formatting with Dockling running locally for highfidelity conversions. Work in a spreadsheet style interface, review documents in bulk, and even ask your AI chat analyst questions across your entire data set. Folio, an AI powered portfolio generator that turns any

sections.title: Foliox
paragraphs: GitHub profile into a stunning modern website in seconds. It fetches your GitHub stats, projects, and contributions, then uses AI to create polished summaries and highlights. Want live project screenshots? Folio grabs them automatically. Customize your URL, integrate LinkedIn, and get SEO optimized metadata for maximum visibility.

sections.title: splintr
paragraphs: Working with LLMs or AI pipelines, but tokenization feels painfully slow. Meet Splinter, a high performance BPE tokenizer built in Rust with Python bindings. It's designed for speed, safety, and efficiency, so you can tokenize massive batches of text without waiting forever. Unlike standard Python tokenizers, Splinter fully leverages multi-core CPUs, giving you serious performance gains for your AI workflows.

sections.title: CC-Switch CLI
paragraphs: Managing multiple LLM CLIs like Claude Code, Codeex, or Gemini can get messy, but CC Switch CLI makes it simple. It's a command line management tool that lets you unify all your AI provider configurations in one place. Switch between MCP servers, manage skills extensions, and control system prompts, all from a single, sleek CLI.

sections.title: PDF Stitcher & Stamp
paragraphs: Need to combine multiple PDFs into one seamless document? PDF Stitcher and Stamp has you covered. With this web app, you can stitch multi-page PDFs into a single continuous image. Choose from vertical, grid, or A4 layouts, and even group pages for easier handling. Want to add a personal touch? Design custom digital stamps and apply them directly to your PDFs.

sections.title: warelay
paragraphs: Managing WhatsApp messages just got a whole lot easier with wear. Send, receive, and even autorely to WhatsApp messages, whether via Twilio or your personal WhatsApp web session. Set up a web hook in one command using Tailscale funnel and configure auto replies with static templates or even AI powered claude commands.

sections.title: Agent Sandbox Skill
paragraphs: Supercharge your AI agents with the agent sandbox skill. Run code, build full stack apps, and automate engineering tasks, all in a fully isolated sandbox, keeping your local machine and production environment safe. Scale effortlessly by running multiple independent agent forks, each with its own secure environment.

sections.title: Whole-Body MPC for Loco-Manipulation
paragraphs: Whole body MPC for local manipulation, a framework that lets robots move and manipulate objects seamlessly. By optimizing joint torques through full body inverse dynamics, this system unifies motion and force planning into a single predictive layer. The result, emergent, physically consistent whole body behaviors that respect dynamics and physical constraints.

sections.title: Blueprint MCP
paragraphs: Blueprint MCP, the smart way to visualize your code bases and system architecture. Generate detailed diagrams instantly using Nano Banana Pro and the Arcade MCP server. Turning complex systems into clear, easy to understand visuals. Seamlessly integrates with Arcad's ecosystem. Pull data from GitHub and more and watch it transform into actionable diagrams.
